hardware: One Apple Silicon Mac, 128 GB unified memory, macOS; router, herd-node and Ollama on the same machine
herd: 0.12.10 from Homebrew (router and herd-node), default settings, telemetry off
method: docs/experiments/idle-keep-alive.py: unload the model, send one request (cold), send another (warm), wait idle_s with no traffic, check /api/ps, send a third. The arms alternate (direct, herd, direct, herd), one at a time on the same Ollama; each run records its repetition and its start time (started_at, UTC). The runs below are one per model and arm (repetition 1), from before start times were recorded. Requests: 'Reply with the word ready.', 8-token cap, temperature 0, streaming; TTFT is the first streamed line.
finding: Ollama unloads a model after 5 idle minutes, so the next direct request reloads it. Herd sends keep_alive -1 on the requests it routes, so through Herd the model was still loaded after the same idle time. The memory stays held until something evicts the model.
